deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This argument controls whether Terraform can destroy the datastore configuration. The default value of DELETE allows unrestricted destructive operations. Deleting a datastore removes the analytics export destination, which could disrupt analytics pipelines and audit data collection across the organization. A generic platform policy can require this to be set to PREVENT, blocking accidental or unauthorized deletion at the platform level without requiring team-specific values.

display_name.description: The display name for the datastore.
display_name.rationale: This is a display name for the datastore. It is purely informational metadata with no effect on where analytics data is exported or how the datastore behaves. Constraining it would not improve security posture.

org_id.description:
The Apigee Organization associated with the Apigee datastore,
in the format 'organizations/{{org_name}}'.
org_id.rationale: This is a reference to the parent Apigee Organization. The value is inherently team- or project-specific. A generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding specific organization identifiers. The security of the organization itself is governed by the google_apigee_organization resource.

target_type.description:
The type of target for the datastore. Must be 'gcs' for Google
Cloud Storage or 'bigquery' for BigQuery.
target_type.rationale: This specifies whether the export destination is Google Cloud Storage (gcs) or BigQuery (bigquery). Both are equally secure GCP-managed services. The choice depends on the team's analytics architecture and data processing requirements. There is no security distinction between the two options.

datastore_config.bucket_name.description: The name of the Cloud Storage bucket. Required for 'gcs' target type.
datastore_config.bucket_name.rationale: This is the name of the GCS bucket used as the export destination. The value is inherently team-specific. The bucket's own security (IAM policies, encryption, access controls) is managed on the google_storage_bucket resource, not by resources that reference it.

datastore_config.dataset_name.description: The name of the BigQuery dataset. Required for 'bigquery' target type.
datastore_config.dataset_name.rationale: This is the name of the BigQuery dataset used as the export destination. The value is inherently team-specific. The dataset's own security (IAM policies, encryption, access controls) is managed on the google_bigquery_dataset resource, not by resources that reference it.

datastore_config.path.description: The path within the Cloud Storage bucket. Used for 'gcs' target type.
datastore_config.path.rationale: This specifies the path within the GCS bucket where exported data is stored. The value is a team-specific organizational choice for how data is structured within the bucket. It has no effect on security posture.

datastore_config.project_id.description: The GCP project ID that the datastore target resides in.
datastore_config.project_id.rationale: This is the GCP project ID where the export destination (bucket or dataset) resides. The value is inherently team-specific. A generic platform policy cannot constrain it without hardcoding specific project identifiers. The project's own security is managed at the project level, not by resources that reference it.

datastore_config.table_prefix.description: The prefix for BigQuery table names. Used for 'bigquery' target type.
datastore_config.table_prefix.rationale: This is a naming prefix for BigQuery tables created during data export. The value is a team-specific organizational choice for table naming conventions. It has no effect on security posture.
